user_questions.question: Should the review summary be (A) generated on demand by a user from the Storefront record page (Einstein Field Generation prompt template on the existing Review_Summary__c field, user reviews and saves; 2 components, no Apex) or (B) regenerated automatically whenever a review is added or changed (record-triggered flow on Review__c plus a prompt template and likely an Apex invocable)? Evidence: Review_Summary__c exists and is blank on all 21 storefronts; no automation exists on either object. Recommendation: A.
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Step 5 says ask only when neither the requirement nor evidence gives a basis; on-demand vs automatic generation changes the component set (flow + Apex vs none) but a recommended default clearly existed, so it is ambiguous whether to ask or decide. I asked; the user had no preference, so the question added nothing.

No guidance for features whose availability depends on a license/setting that cannot be queried (Prompt Builder / Field Generation; GenAiPromptTemplate is not queryable). I applied the 'Conditional on license' rule from org-verification.md to both rows, but the second row (FlexiPage) is only conditional transitively, and the spec-format rules do not say whether dependent rows must also be Conditional.

The spec-format 'Module' rule lists no standard folder for GenAiPromptTemplate; I used force-app/main/default/genAiPromptTemplates (the standard source folder), but the rule's examples do not cover it.

Permission set assignment (EinsteinGPTPromptTemplateUser, platform-owned, 0 assignees) is needed for delivery but is neither metadata nor editable; the skill covers 'undeliverable responsibility' but not setup steps like assignments, so I recorded it as blocking for delivery in Section 8.

AskCoworker repeatedly tagged facts I sent as '[Verified: prior session]' and invented an OD with a new field; the response table covers this (echoed facts / drop unrequested behavior), which worked as intended.
